citation: Waaler J, Machon O, von Kries JP, Wilson SR, Lundenes E, Wedlich D, Gradl D, Paulsen JE, Machonova O, Dembinski JL, Dinh H, Krauss S. Novel synthetic antagonists of canonical Wnt signaling inhibit colorectal cancer cell growth. Cancer Research. 2011. doi:10.1158/0008-5472.CAN-10-1282.
description: This paper inhibited canonical Wnt signaling at the beta-catenin destruction complex, reduced active beta-catenin, and down-regulated AXIN2, SP5, and NKD1; it also tested JW74 in Apc(Min) mice. It supports the expectation that loss of APC, a negative regulator of beta-catenin, should increase canonical Wnt target genes such as Axin2 and Nkd1.

citation: Liu XH, Zhang ZY, Andersson KB, Husberg C, Enger UH, Raeder MG, Christensen G, Louch WE. Cardiomyocyte-specific disruption of Serca2 in adult mice causes sarco(endo)plasmic reticulum stress and apoptosis. Cell Calcium. 2010. doi:10.1016/j.ceca.2010.09.009.
description: Adult mouse cardiomyocyte Serca2 disruption induced unfolded-protein-response and pro-apoptotic markers including PERK/eIF2alpha, CHOP/DDIT3, caspase 12, and Bax. It supports the directionally interpretable expectation that Atp2a2 loss can increase ER-stress and CHOP-associated transcripts.

citation: Li H, Min Q, Ouyang C, Lee J, He C, Zou MH, Xie Z. AMPK activation prevents excess nutrient-induced hepatic lipid accumulation by inhibiting mTORC1 signaling and endoplasmic reticulum stress response. Biochimica et Biophysica Acta. 2014. doi:10.1016/j.bbadis.2014.07.002.
description: This study found that ER-stress and lipid accumulation in HepG2 cells were associated with mTORC1 activation and that mTORC1 inhibition attenuated responses induced by high glucose or by TSC2 deletion. It supports the expectation that loss of the mTORC1 inhibitor Tsc2 can increase lipid/cholesterol and ER-stress output genes.

citation: Waszak SM, Robinson GW, Gudenas BL, Smith KS, Forget A, Kojic M, Garcia-Lopez J, Hadley J, Hamilton KV, Indersie E, Buchhalter I, Kerssemakers J, Jaeger N, Sharma T, Rausch T, Kool M, Sturm D, Jones DTW, Vasilyeva A, Tatevossian RG, Neale G, Lombard B, Loew D, Nakitandwe J, Rusch M, Bowers DC, Bendel A, Partap S, Chintagumpala M, Crawford J, Gottardo NG, Smith A, Dufour C, Rutkowski S, Eggen T, Wesenberg F, Kjaerheim K, Feychting M, Lannering B, Schuez J, Johansen C, Andersen TV, Roosli M, Kuehni CE, Grotzer M, Remke M, Puget S, Pajtler KW, Milde T, Witt O, Ryzhova M, Korshunov A, Orr BA, Ellison DW, Brugieres L, Lichter P, Nichols KE, Gajjar A, Wainwright BJ, Ayrault O, Korbel JO, Northcott PA, Pfister SM. Germline Elongator mutations in Sonic Hedgehog medulloblastoma. Nature. 2020. doi:10.1038/s41586-020-2164-5.
description: ELP1-associated Sonic Hedgehog medulloblastomas showed biallelic ELP1 inactivation, destabilization of the Elongator complex, loss of Elongator-dependent tRNA modifications, translational reprogramming, and unfolded-protein-response induction. It supports a target-specific ELP1-to-proteostasis-stress relationship and an indirect Elongator-complex bridge for ELP2.

citation: Ferrer CM, Lynch TP, Sodi VL, Falcone JN, Schwab LP, Peacock DL, Vocadlo DJ, Seagroves TN, Reginato MJ. O-GlcNAcylation regulates cancer metabolism and survival stress signaling via regulation of the HIF-1 pathway. Molecular Cell. 2014. doi:10.1016/j.molcel.2014.04.026.
description: This study placed the hexosamine biosynthetic pathway upstream of OGT/O-GlcNAcylation and found that reducing O-GlcNAcylation activated ER stress and CHOP-mediated apoptosis. It supplies a mechanistic bridge from Gfpt1 loss to CHOP/ER-stress transcripts.

citation: Jang I, Kim HB, Seo H, Kim JY, Choi H, Yoo JS, Kim JW, Cho JW. O-GlcNAcylation of eIF2alpha regulates the phospho-eIF2alpha-mediated ER stress response. Biochimica et Biophysica Acta. 2015. doi:10.1016/j.bbamcr.2015.04.017.
description: The paper showed that O-GlcNAcylation of eIF2alpha modulates stress-induced eIF2alpha phosphorylation, CHOP expression, and apoptosis. It makes the Gfpt1-to-hexosamine-to-O-GlcNAc bridge biologically specific but still indirect for the observed neuronal response.

citation: Nam YJ, Kim A, Lee MS, Shin YK, Sohn DS, Lee CS. Lamotrigine attenuates proteasome inhibition-induced apoptosis by suppressing the activation of the mitochondrial pathway and the caspase-8- and Bid-dependent pathways. Neurochemical Research. 2016. doi:10.1007/s11064-016-1962-5.
description: Proteasome inhibitors in differentiated PC12 and SH-SY5Y cells increased Bax and p53 and activated apoptotic mitochondrial and caspase pathways. It gives a complex-level expectation that impairing the 26S proteasome through Psmc1 or Psmc5 loss can increase Bax/autophagy-stress outputs, but it is pharmacologic rather than target-specific genetic evidence.

citation: Altaf F, Vesely C, Sheikh AM, Munir R, Shah STA, Tariq A. Modulation of ADAR mRNA expression in patients with congenital heart defects. PLoS One. 2019. doi:10.1371/journal.pone.0200968.
description: The study identified FLNB as an ADAR2-regulated transcript in mouse heart and found that Adar2 loss dramatically reduced Flnb RNA editing without changing total Flnb mRNA abundance. It is directly relevant to repeated Flnb decreases after Adarb1 perturbation, but it does not predict the observed expression direction.

citation: Yuskaitis CJ, Rossitto LA, Gurnani S, Bainbridge E, Poduri A, Sahin M. Chronic mTORC1 inhibition rescues behavioral and biochemical deficits resulting from neuronal Depdc5 loss in mice. Human Molecular Genetics. 2019. doi:10.1093/hmg/ddz123.
description: Neuronal Depdc5 knockout mice had mTORC1 hyperactivation, enlarged brains and neurons, and partial rescue by rapamycin. It supplies the target-specific first step from Depdc5 loss to mTORC1 signaling, which can be connected indirectly to lipid/ER-stress genes through Tsc2/mTORC1 literature.
